# Move release to Monday

## Current state

[notes.md](notes.md) defines the only tracked schedule in this repo:

```1:2:notes.md
The release ships on Friday.
QA signs off on Thursday.
```

There are no CI configs, calendars, or automation elsewhere in the workspace—any operational follow-through lives outside this repo.

**Calendar context (from session date):** Today is **Friday, Oct 30, 2026**. Under the current notes, QA was **Thursday, Oct 29** and release was **today**. Moving “the release” to Monday means **Monday, Nov 3, 2026** for this cycle unless you intend a standing weekly change (see decision below).

## Recommended schedule change (keeps QA → ship gap)

| Milestone | Before | After |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| QA sign-off | Thursday | **Friday** (business day before Monday ship) |
| Release | Friday | **Monday** |

This preserves a single full business day between sign-off and production ship (Thursday→Friday becomes Friday→Monday, with the weekend in between—same pattern teams use for Monday releases).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before [Current cadence]
    QA_Thu[QA Thursday]
    Ship_Fri[Release Friday]
    QA_Thu --> Ship_Fri
  end
  subgraph after [Monday cadence]
    QA_Fri[QA Friday]
    Ship_Mon[Release Monday]
    QA_Fri --> Ship_Mon
  end
```

## Decision to confirm before editing

**One-time slip (this release only)** vs **permanent cadence (every release on Monday)**:

- **One-time slip:** Change [notes.md](notes.md) only if you want the repo to reflect the new default; otherwise keep notes as policy and handle this week via comms/tickets. Still run the “this cycle” checklist below.
- **Permanent cadence:** Update [notes.md](notes.md) to Monday/Friday permanently (single file change in this repo).

Default assumption in the steps below: **permanent cadence update** in `notes.md`, since that is the only artifact here.

## Planned file change (after you approve execution)

Update [notes.md](notes.md) to:

```markdown
The release ships on Monday.
QA signs off on Friday.
```

No other files exist to modify in this workspace.

## This-cycle operational checklist (outside repo)

Because the original release day is **today (Friday)** and the new target is **Monday, Nov 3**:

1. **Announce the slip** — Stakeholders, support, and anyone on a Friday release checklist should get a short note: new ship date **Mon Nov 3**, reason, and whether the Friday window is cancelled.
2. **QA timing** — If sign-off already happened **Thu Oct 29** for a **Fri Oct 30** ship:
   - Treat **Mon Nov 3** as a new ship boundary: schedule **regression / re-sign-off on Fri Oct 31** (or explicit written acceptance that Thu sign-off still covers Mon ship).
   - Avoid “silent” extension without QA acknowledgment—three extra days can pick up new merges or env drift.
3. **Freeze and branch policy** — Clarify whether code freeze moves with the date (e.g. freeze through Fri Oct 31, ship Mon) or stays as-is.
4. **Monday logistics** — On-call, deployment window, customer comms, and rollback owners for **Mon Nov 3** (Monday releases often need explicit coverage vs Friday habits).
5. **Downstream calendars** — Update any external systems (team calendar, release ticket, status page) not represented in this repo.

## Verification

- [notes.md](notes.md) text matches Monday / Friday after edit.
- Stakeholders have the new date and QA plan in writing.
- For this cycle: confirmed whether **Fri Oct 31** re-sign-off is required before **Mon Nov 3** ship.

## Scope limits

This plan does **not** change any files until you exit plan mode and approve execution. There is nothing else in the project tree to search or reconfigure for release automation.
